test: RL-9' definitive stale-harm A/B (blind, K=5/arm, mechanically graded, retrieval-gated)
mechanism: 61 blind subagent calls; 4 real ResearchLoop corrections x {clean, hardneg, closedbook} x 5 runs; all 4 hardneg patches passed the retrieval gate (both stale+current present)
headline: 6/20 hard-negative runs harmed (stale answer); worst case 5/5

tables (12->10, non-inferable, stale ran.verdict: MEMORY FLIPPED A SAFE ABSTENTION INTO A CONFIDENT WRONG ANSWER

trigger (v2->v4, INFERABLE, stale #1).verdict: no harm; model prior aligned + recognized 'deprecated'

interpretation: Memory CAN actively mislead a real model, not just coexist in the patch. Harm is concentrated where (a) the stale fact ranks at/above the current one AND (b) the two are directly contradictory atomic values with no 'deprecated/old' cue. This OVERTURNS the earlier single-run read ('model recovered') -- recovery is not reliable; it depends on rank order, contradiction type, and model priors. contextgit does no disambiguation, so it relies on cues (rank, 'deprecated' wording) that it doesn't control.
grading_caveat: Mechanical substring grader. tables/trigger 'clean'/'both' classifications are partly artifacts (a correct answer like 'no profiles table' contains the stale marker 'profiles table'; a correct trigger answer mentions the deprecated 'v2 defineJob'). Hand-reading the sample answers confirms: tables-hardneg 5/5 are genuinely WRONG ('12 tables...'); trigger is genuinely correct (harm 0); clean arms are correct. Net genuine harm ~6/20, concentrated in tables.
closed_book_confirms_non_inferable: reconcile/guardrails/tables: closed-book abstains or can't answer -> memory is genuinely needed, so a stale-flip is real damage (not the model ignoring memory it didn't need). trigger is inferable (control).
